definitions.explanation: The polite form of {店|みせ}. Refers to any retail shop, restaurant, or similar establishment. Very commonly used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧お{店|みせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}っています→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you know a good restaurant?

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧お{店|みせ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: A new shop opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧お{店|みせ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{手頃|てごろ}→手頃：04068_tegoro⟧で、⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{来|く}ます→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: This restaurant has reasonable prices and good food, so I come here often.

notes:
The polite prefix お attached to ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧ (shop/store). In everyday Japanese, お{店|みせ} is far more common than plain ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧, especially when speaking. It can refer to any type of commercial establishment — retail shops, restaurants, bars, cafes, etc.

USAGE:
While ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧ on its own can sound blunt, お{店|みせ} is the standard conversational form. Using ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧ without お is more common in compound words (⟦{店員|てんいん}→店員：00897_tenin⟧, ⟦{店長|てんちょう}→店長：30461_tenchou⟧) or when used as a suffix (⟦{花屋|はなや}→花屋：03136_hanaya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{店|みせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to open a shop
- お{店|みせ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}す→探す：00493_sagasu⟧: to look for a restaurant/shop
- お{店|みせ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: shop staff; restaurant staff

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{店舗|てんぽ}→店舗：12481_tenpo⟧: store; shop premises — more formal/commercial
- ⟦ショップ→ショップ：08913_shoppu⟧: shop — borrowed from English, often for specialty or trendy stores
- ⟦{商店|しょうてん}→商店：11841_shouten⟧: shop; store — more traditional, often in ⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧ (shopping street)
